name: Westwood Bl, Le Conte Av to the E Line (Westwood/Rancho Park station)
source: Path from the LA Metro GTFS shape for line 761 (shape 7610078_JUNE26) from Le Conte Av to Olympic Bl, and from TomTom traffic-flow road geometry from Olympic Bl to the E Line crossing (2026-11-19).
notes: LADOT's Westwood Boulevard Safety and Mobility Project (Council District 5) proposes Class IV protected bike lanes (2.2 mi), bus-only lanes (1.1 mi, LADOT estimates buses 14 to 20% faster) with boarding platforms, and pedestrian safety work, connecting UCLA with the Metro E Line and the future D Line station at Wilshire Bl. LADOT estimates car travel could take up to 1 minute 50 seconds more per mile at the busiest times; 75 to 80% of on-street parking kept; 73 part-time spaces between Santa Monica Bl and Pico Bl become 63 all-day spaces. The project page does not give exact extents or which 1.1 mi gets bus lanes; this corridor uses Le Conte Av to the E Line crossing (about 2.2 mi, matching the bike-lane length). Metro lines 761 and 233 stop on Westwood Bl only from Le Conte Av to Santa Monica Bl (761's next stop is Sepulveda / Pico; it leaves Westwood near Olympic Bl), so timetable and Cal-ITP speeds cover sections S1 and S2 only. Santa Monica Bl to the E Line is served by Big Blue Bus, which this project does not collect (the Swiftly key covers LA Metro only; other agencies return 403), so sections S3 and S4 have general-traffic data only. TomTom's first snapshot (2026-11-19) had no northbound piece through Westwood Village (Le Conte Av to Wilshire Bl); re-check after a few days. The project overlaps the Pico Bl corridor in name only: it crosses Pico Bl about 6 mi west of the Pico project. Facts from the LADOT project page text supplied by the owner on 2026-11-19.
